complexity.notes: Two performance issues, neither affecting correctness: pop(0) on a list costs O(queue length) per pop where collections.deque.popleft() is O(1), and nodes are only marked visited when dequeued, so a node is enqueued once per neighbor processed before it, letting the queue hold O(E) entries. On dense graphs this degrades the traversal to O(E^2) (Theta(n^4) in node count on a complete graph); adding nodes to a visited set at enqueue time restores O(V + E). The second pass building neighbor lists is clean and the empty-graph case is handled.
complexity.summary: BFS from the start node, creating a blank clone for each original node in a dict keyed by the original node (identity hash), then a second pass wires up each clone's neighbor list through the old-to-new map.
